Things to think about before you replace a fence

  • Who owns the fence? Check your property deeds, and have a quick chat with your neighbour before work starts. It saves disagreements later.
  • Height – in most cases a garden fence can be up to 2 metres high without planning permission, or 1 metre next to a road or footpath. Rules can differ for listed buildings and some conservation areas, so check if that applies to you [PLACEHOLDER: confirm planning wording].
  • Combining jobs – if you are also planning a patio, turf or a new driveway, doing it together can save time and disruption.

Fencing FAQs

How much does a new fence cost?

It depends on the length and height of the fence, whether old fencing needs removing and access to your garden. We will give you a free, no-obligation quote after a quick visit.

How long does it take to put up a fence?

Most garden fences are finished in a day or two [PLACEHOLDER: confirm typical fencing duration].

Do I need planning permission for a new fence?

Usually not, if it is no higher than 2 metres (or 1 metre next to a road or footpath). Listed buildings and some conservation areas have extra rules [PLACEHOLDER: confirm planning wording].
